# Abhisamaya Saṁyutta (SN 13)

**ID:** SN 13
**Section:** Saṁyuttanikāya (sn)
**Collection:** Suttas-Early-1
**Title (Pali):** Abhisamaya Saṁyutta
**Title (English, SuttaCentral):** Linked Discourses on Comprehension
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/sn13

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Abhisamaya Saṁyutta* (SN 13), rendered in English as the "Linked Discourses on Comprehension" [SuttaCentral] or "Connected Discourses on the Breakthrough" [Bodhi 2003], is the thirteenth collection of the *Saṁyuttanikāya*, situated between the *Nidānasaṁyutta* and the *Dhātusaṁyutta* [Bodhi 2003]. While the Burmese and Pali Text Society traditions count 56 *saṁyuttas* and present this text as an independent chapter containing 11 discourses without subdivision into vaggas, the Sinhalese manuscript tradition incorporates it as a subchapter (*vagga*) of the preceding *Nidānasaṁyutta* [Bodhi 2003_x]. Modern scholars note that this Sinhalese subsumption lacks thematic justification, as the suttas make no mention of dependent origination (*paṭiccasamuppāda*) or causal chains [Bodhi 2003_x]. SuttaCentral's database enumerates 12 individual suttas within the file [SuttaCentral].

Doctrinally, *abhisamaya* signifies the "breakthrough" or "penetration" to the four noble truths [Bodhi 2003; Liew 2009]. In the commentary (*Sāratthappakāsinī*), *abhisametāvino* is glossed as abiding having broken through to the noble truths by wisdom (*paññāya ariyasaccāni abhisametvā ṭhitassa*), describing a person endowed with right view (*diṭṭhisampanna*) who has attained stream-entry [Bodhi 2003]. Each sutta in the collection illustrates the momentous spiritual impact of realizing the Dhamma through vivid recurring similes [SuttaCentral], such as comparing a tiny pinch of dust held on the Buddha's fingernail (*Nakhasikhāsutta*) or droplets of water at the confluence of great rivers with the vast mass of the earth or the ocean; these similes demonstrate that for a noble disciple who has achieved breakthrough, the suffering left to endure is negligible compared to the immeasurable suffering already extinguished [Bodhi 2003; Bodhi 2003_x; Hazra 1994].

Curated parallels recorded on SuttaCentral include a direct Chinese parallel in the *Saṁyuktāgama* (SĀ 439 for SN 13.11 *Tatiyapabbatasutta*) [SuttaCentral]. Computational text-reuse analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal sharing (1,727 matches across 36 texts), most heavily overlapping in formulaic passages with the *Sacca Saṁyutta* (SN 56, with over 520 matches), *Dhātu Saṁyutta* (SN 14), and *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12) [DharmaNexus]. DharmaNexus also detects cross-language alignments with the alternative Chinese *Saṁyuktāgama* (*Bieyi za ahan jing*, T 100) and formulaic parallels across several Mahāyāna treatises preserved in Tibetan and Sanskrit [DharmaNexus].
